<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <groupId>com.example</groupId>
    <artifactId>app</artifactId>
    <version>1.0.0-SNAPSHOT</version>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <properties>
        <maven.compiler.release>21</maven.compiler.release>
        <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>

        <slf4j.version>2.0.20</slf4j.version>
        <logback.version>1.6.5</logback.version>
        <junit.version>6.1.3</junit.version>
    </properties>

    <dependencies>
        <!-- Logging facade: the only logging API application code compiles against. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.slf4j</groupId>
            <artifactId>slf4j-api</artifactId>
            <version>${slf4j.version}</version>
        </dependency>

        <!-- Logging backend: runtime scope keeps it off the compile classpath,
             so code can't accidentally depend on Logback classes. Swap this
             for any other SLF4J provider (e.g. slf4j-simple, log4j-slf4j2-impl). -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>ch.qos.logback</groupId>
            <artifactId>logback-classic</artifactId>
            <version>${logback.version}</version>
            <scope>runtime</scope>
        </dependency>

        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <version>${junit.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.16.0</version>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>3.6.0</version>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>
EOF
cat > src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app;

import org.slf4j.Logger;
import org.slf4j.LoggerFactory;

public class App {

    private static final Logger log = LoggerFactory.getLogger(App.class);

    public static void main(String[] args) {
        log.info("Application starting with {} argument(s)", args.length);
        System.out.println(new App().greet("world"));
        log.info("Application finished");
    }

    public String greet(String name) {
        log.debug("Greeting {}", name);
        return "Hello, " + name + "!";
    }
}
EOF
cat > src/main/resources/logback.xml <<'EOF'
<configuration>
    <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">
        <encoder>
            <pattern>%d{HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>
        </encoder>
    </appender>

    <logger name="com.example" level="DEBUG"/>

    <root level="INFO">
        <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE"/>
    </root>
</configuration>
EOF
cat > src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java <<'EOF'
package com.example.app;

import static org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.assertEquals;

import org.junit.jupiter.api.Test;

class AppTest {

    @Test
    void greetsByName() {
        assertEquals("Hello, world!", new App().greet("world"));
    }
}
EOF
cat > .gitignore <<'EOF'
target/
EOF
mvn -q -B package 2>&1 | tail -30 && java -cp "target/classes:$(mvn -q -B dependency:build-classpath -Dmdep.outputFile=/dev/stdout -Dmdep.includeScope=runtime)" com.example.app.App

content.text:
I've set up the project in `/work`. It uses **SLF4J** as the logging facade, so the application code only depends on the SLF4J API and not on any particular logging library. `mvn package` builds it and the test passes, and running the app prints log lines through the backend.

**What's in it**
- `pom.xml`
  - `org.slf4j:slf4j-api` 2.0.20 is the only logging library the code compiles against.
  - `ch.qos.logback:logback-classic` 1.6.5 is the backend that actually writes the logs. It's in **`runtime` scope**, so code that imports a Logback class won't compile. That keeps the code tied to the facade only.
  - JUnit Jupiter 6.1.3 for tests, compiler plugin 3.16.0 and surefire 3.6.0, targeting Java 21. These were the latest stable versions on Maven Central.
- `src/main/java/com/example/app/App.java`: a small example that logs through `LoggerFactory.getLogger(...)`, using `{}` placeholders in messages.
- `src/main/resources/logback.xml`: logs to the console, at DEBUG for `com.example` and INFO for everything else.
- `src/test/java/com/example/app/AppTest.java`: one example test.
- `.gitignore`: ignores `target/`.

**Switching the backend:** replace the `logback-classic` dependency with another SLF4J backend, such as `org.slf4j:slf4j-simple` or `org.apache.logging.log4j:log4j-slf4j2-impl`, and replace `logback.xml` with that backend's config file. The Java code stays the same.

I used `com.example:app` as a placeholder group and artifact ID, so rename it as needed. Nothing has been committed. I didn't touch the existing `stderr.log` and `transcript.jsonl` files.
